title.narrative: Provision of integrated life-saving emergency health care nutrition interventions to drought response in the Xudur Tiyeglow Districts of Bakol, Somalia.

description.narrative: ltpgtXudur and Tayeeglow districts in Bakool Region, South Central Somalia, are among the areas most severely affected by recurrent drought, protracted conflict, displacement, and chronic underinvestment in basic social services. The convergence of these shocks has critically undermined household coping capacities, especially in rural and hard-to-reach villages, driving sharp deterioration in health and nutrition indicators. Five consecutive failed or underperforming rainy seasons (2020-2025) have triggered catastrophic livestock mortality (40-60%), near-total crop failure (87% reduction), and massive internal displacement (85,000 IDPs in Xudur, 42,000 in Tayeeglow). The FSNAU post-Gu nutrition assessment (September 2025) documented critical levels of acute malnutrition: Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) rates of 18.2% in Xudur and 19.7% in Tayeeglow, both far exceeding the WHO emergency threshold of 15%. Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) prevalence stands at 3.8% in Xudur and 4.2% in Tayeeglow. Under-five crude mortality rates have reached 1.2 deaths/10,000/day, exceeding emergency thresholds. The October 2025 IPC analysis classified 67% of the population in both districts as facing Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse acute food insecurity, with 18,000 people in Xudur and 12,000 in Tayeeglow in Emergency (IPC Phase 4). Nationally, food insecurity is projected to affect 4.4 million Somalis between October 2025 and March 2026. The existing health system has collapsed under crisis pressure. In Xudur, only one district hospital (Sheikh Aweys) and five primary health centers are partially functional, operating at less than 30% of MoH-recommended capacity. In Tayeeglow, only the Stabilization Center and one health post remain operational. Facilities face severe staff shortages, prolonged medicine stock-outs, non-functional cold chains, and compromised infrastructure. Less than 35% of the population has access to basic primary health care within 5 km. Measles vaccination coverage stands at only 41%, anemia affects 62% of pregnant women, and only 28% of pregnant women attend at least one ANC visit. MARDO's Health and Nutrition Program aims to provide integrated life-saving and sustaining health and nutrition support to the most vulnerable drought-affected populations in the Xudur and Tayeeglow
